channel.title: Otago Daily Times - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Otago Daily Times (odt.co.nz)

item.title: Call to stop 'derogatory' comments about councils
item.description: Pita Tipene said he wouldn't quote the 'derogatory comments' made by Cabinet Ministers. Photo: RNZ By Anneke Smith of RNZ Northland Regional Council chairperson Pita Tipene has called on Cabinet Ministers to stop making "derogatory" comments about councils.

item.title: Park’s future put into long-term plan
item.description: The Southland Stags train at Rugby Park. There has been mixed reactions on whether spending money to upgrade Rugby Park is the best solution for the facility.

item.title: Woodman-Wickliffe says she's ready to retire
item.description: Portia Woodman-Wickliffe has again announced she is bowing out of international rugby. Photo: Getty Images The greatest of all time is hanging up her black jersey, again.

item.title: Museum steel not made with coal: council
item.description: An artist’s view of Te Unua Museum of Southland. IMAGE: SUPPLIED Invercargill City Council has moved to ensure coal dust will not be settling on its new four-star green award for the Te Unua Museum.

item.title: Girls’ high fundraising for revamp of reception area
item.description: Southland Girls’ High School student services reception team of (from left) Margaret Flannery, Pauline Kingsland and Sharon Ridden are looking forward to a new reception area. Southland Girls’ High School has launched a $1 million fundraising effort to develop its reception into a modern student sciences area.

item.title: Sausage-makers set to snag title
item.description: Tui Base Camp is the home of the Tuatapere Sausage. Tuatapere — fire up the barbecues and tighten your apron strings because some top-notch butchers are in town today competing for the Best New World Sausage crown.

item.title: Wrestlers to clash in Fight for Gold
item.description: Southern Pro Wrestling athletes Hayden ‘Cool Guy Sky’ Jackson (left) and Sam ‘Azza’ Schroeder get into character at the Bill Richardson Transport World. PHOTO: SUPPLIED Southern Power Wrestling (SPW) is back for another year of wild, lycra-clad men turning up the tumbles in the ring.

item.title: Club launches venue rebrand
item.description: The Riff club president Trevor Daley. They might be getting a name change, but the music will always stay the same.

item.title: Man due in court after service station incident
item.description: Armed police were called to the Z service station on Wednesday night. Photo: Gregor Richardson A man charged after recent offences in the Otago coastal area is due in court on Friday, police say.

item.title: Another IT outage hits hospitals
item.description: Photo: RNZ By Ellen O'Dwyer of RNZ Auckland and Northland hospitals have been hit by IT problems today.
